summary: Recombinant human luteinizing hormone (lutropin alfa, Luveris) is a gonadotropin produced in genetically engineered Chinese hamster ovary cells. It is used together with recombinant FSH (follitropin alfa) to stimulate follicular development in women with severe LH and FSH deficiency (hypogonadotropic hypogonadism). LH provides the receptor stimulus needed for adequate estradiol production and follicular maturation. The principal risks are ovarian hyperstimulation syndrome (OHSS), multiple pregnancy, and local injection reactions. It is authorised in the EU (EMA) and is approved as a biologic for assisted reproduction; this record draws on the EMA SmPC/BNF as the primary source.
indications: Stimulation of follicular development in combination with follicle-stimulating hormone (FSH) in women with severe LH and FSH deficiency (endogenous serum LH below 1.2 IU/L)
Used as part of assisted reproductive technology / ovulation induction in hypogonadotropic hypogonadism

dosage.d: Lutropin alfa 75 IU SC daily together with follitropin alfa 75-150 IU SC daily
dosage.n: Individualise by ovarian response monitored on ultrasound and estradiol

dosage.d: Withhold gonadotropins and give hCG to trigger ovulation when follicles are mature
dosage.n: Withhold hCG if excessive ovarian response to reduce OHSS risk

admin: Reconstitute the powder with the supplied solvent and use immediately; the solution should be clear
Inject subcutaneously, usually together with follitropin alfa (may be co-administered)
First injection should be under direct medical supervision; rotate injection sites
Administer under the supervision of a physician experienced in fertility treatment
moa: Lutropin alfa is recombinant human luteinizing hormone that binds LH receptors on ovarian theca and granulosa cells. In women with severe gonadotropin deficiency it supplies the LH activity needed, alongside FSH, to support follicular estradiol synthesis and drive follicular maturation, enabling subsequent ovulation when triggered with hCG.

absolute: Hypersensitivity to lutropin alfa or any excipient
Tumours of the hypothalamus or pituitary gland
Ovarian enlargement or cyst not due to polycystic ovarian disease and of unknown origin
Conditions incompatible with pregnancy (e.g., primary ovarian failure, malformations of sexual organs, fibroid tumours incompatible with pregnancy)
monitor: Ovarian response by ultrasound and serum estradiol

preg: Lutropin alfa is not indicated during pregnancy and treatment is stopped once pregnancy is confirmed. There is no indication for continued use; any pregnancy achieved should be managed obstetrically with attention to the increased risk of multiple gestation.
lact: There is no indication for use during breastfeeding. Lutropin alfa is not used in lactating women.
renal: No specific dosing data in renal impairment are provided; use under specialist supervision with individualised dosing.
hepatic: No specific dosing data in hepatic impairment are provided; use under specialist supervision with individualised dosing.

moderate: Concurrent use with other gonadotropins (FSH, hCG) is intended therapy - additive ovarian stimulation requires careful monitoring for OHSS
minor: No clinically significant minor interactions reported
interactions.diagnostics: Cross-reacts with hCG in immunoassays; gonadotropin levels measured during treatment reflect administered drug

common: Injection site reactions (pain, redness, bruising, swelling)
serious: Moderate to severe ovarian hyperstimulation syndrome (OHSS)
rare: Adnexal torsion as a complication of ovarian enlargement
emergency: Severe OHSS with ascites, dyspnea, oliguria or thromboembolism
Ovarian torsion with acute abdominal pain

monitoring: Transvaginal ovarian ultrasound to track follicle number and size
Clinical signs and symptoms of OHSS (abdominal distension, weight gain, dyspnea)
Signs of thromboembolism in at-risk women
counsel: This treatment is given by injection under the skin as part of a fertility programme
Report severe abdominal pain or swelling, breathlessness, marked weight gain, or reduced urine output - these may signal ovarian hyperstimulation
Be aware of the increased chance of a multiple pregnancy (twins or more)
Attend all scheduled scans and blood tests so your dose can be adjusted
Tell your doctor about leg pain/swelling or chest symptoms that could indicate a clot
pk: Stimulation effect develops over the days of dosing
Serum LH peak approximately 4-16 hours after subcutaneous injection
Terminal half-life approximately 10-12 hours after repeated dosing
Daily dosing maintains LH activity throughout the stimulation cycle
Store refrigerated 2-8 C; use reconstituted solution immediately and protect from light per the SmPC
pearls: Not FDA-approved as a standalone product in current US labeling; authorised in the EU as Luveris - this record is based on the EMA SmPC and BNF as the primary source
Lutropin alfa supplies LH activity for women with profound LH/FSH deficiency (endogenous LH <1.2 IU/L) - it is given alongside FSH, not alone
Withhold the hCG trigger when there is an excessive ovarian response to lower the risk of severe OHSS
Counsel couples about the substantially increased rate of multiple pregnancy with gonadotropin stimulation
Treatment must be supervised by a clinician experienced in infertility management with ultrasound/estradiol monitoring
missed: Doses are scheduled as part of a closely monitored stimulation cycle. If an injection is missed, contact the fertility clinic for advice rather than altering the schedule yourself - do not double the dose.
overdose: The effects of overdose are not established but excessive dosing is expected to provoke ovarian hyperstimulation syndrome. Management is supportive: withhold further gonadotropin, monitor for and treat OHSS (fluid balance, thromboprophylaxis, drainage of ascites if severe), and withhold the hCG trigger.
